page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance within the c4 family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by an L3 cache of 504 MB. The instance is equipped with 248.0 GB of RAM, translating to 7.75 GB of memory per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 1745 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity spread across 5 drives. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in single-core and multi-core operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2307.0, which is in the top tier, and a multi-core score of 18257.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 36.83 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered at 235.62 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show 2702.38 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 168.46 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For database operations, the server processed 62.26 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside a Passmark database score of 17024.29. LLM inference benchmarks for a medium 7B model yielded 195.69 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 25.76 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-32-lssd offers a high-density memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with fast local NVMe storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads. This balance makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, and data processing pipelines. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, enhances its suitability for CPU-based machine learning inference and cryptographic operations. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and localized data analytics.
